AfterCombatEnd.rationale: FishingRod.cs:42-59 maps clause for clause: the `room.Encounter.RoomType != RoomType.Monster` bail is `if room_type != RoomType.MONSTER: return` (fishing_rod.py:23-24, executed -- an ELITE combat leaves combats_seen at 0); `CombatsSeen++` then `% Combats == 0` is fishing_rod.py:25-26 with COMBATS = 3 from DynamicVar('Combats', 3m) (FishingRod.cs:40) and no AscensionHelper branch in the file; the candidate set `PileType.Deck.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable)` is `[c for c in run.deck if c.is_upgradable]` (fishing_rod.py:27) in the same deck order; `RunState.Rng.Niche.NextItem(items)` is `run.rng_set.niche.next_item(upgradable)` (fishing_rod.py:31) on the same run-level stream; and C#'s `if (cardModel != null)` empty-list guard is `if upgradable` (fishing_rod.py:28). Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): four Monster combats give combats_seen 1,2,3,4 with exactly one deck card upgraded, on the third.

guards.what: N1: `CombatsSeen` is written only in AfterCombatEnd and never reset -- sweep-reset lists fishing_rod among the 32 relics that never reset a mid-combat field, with 'C# resets: [AfterCombatEnd]'
guards.rationale: The sweep's 'C# resets' column is an AST fact about which combat-boundary hooks the C# relic OVERRIDES, not about what those hooks do -- FishingRod.AfterCombatEnd (FishingRod.cs:42-59) INCREMENTS the counter, it does not clear it, and nothing anywhere in FishingRod.cs assigns CombatsSeen = 0. The field is a per-RUN counter on both sides (C# marks it [SavedProperty], FishingRod.cs:25, i.e. it is meant to survive save/load), and `sweep-reset-exec` puts it in the 13 of 16 executed candidates that agree with a freshly constructed instance. Confirmed independently by execution here (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`). This entry exists because the batch brief listed fishing_rod as a Sweep A candidate 'C# resets at AfterCombatEnd' -- that reading is wrong, and settling it by execution rather than by reading is binding rule 5.

guards.what: N2: `CardCmd.Upgrade(cardModel)` is called on a card the Where clause already filtered to IsUpgradable, and the sim's `.upgrade()` (cards/base.py:146-147) is unguarded
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 14 / sweep D: the sim's Card.upgrade() has no IsUpgradable guard, so every caller must supply its own. fishing_rod.py:27 builds the candidate list with `if c.is_upgradable` BEFORE the pick, so the class-14 hit is closed at this site. Sweep D's own published correction names fishing_rod as one of five sites its first 3-line-window version over-reported for exactly this reason; recorded here so the confirmation is on the record rather than in the sweep's footnote.

guards.what: N3: RunState.finish_combat dispatches after_combat_end only when `room_type is not None and not self.is_dead` (run.py:1207); C#'s guard is structural
guards.rationale: Hook.AfterCombatEnd is reached only from CombatManager's victory path (EndCombatInternal), so a lost combat fires no relic hook at all -- the same fact audit/records/relic/chosen_cheese-era batch-3 probe work recorded for AfterCombatEnd generally. The sim's `not self.is_dead` guard stands in for it, and a combat the sim ends with player_won=False is itself gated on player death, so the two agree. NOTE per binding rule 7: run.py and CombatManager.cs are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: the legacy branch `run.rng.choice(upgradable)` (fishing_rod.py:33) when run.rng_set is None -- a different stream from Rng.Niche
guards.rationale: The port carries both arms explicitly: the parity arm uses the run-level Niche stream the source names, and the legacy arm keeps the shared random.Random so pre-SP2 sim seeds stay byte-for-byte reproducible. This is the sim's established two-arm house style for named RNG streams (PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half), and the observable -- which card gets upgraded -- is identical in distribution; only a parity run against a recording can tell them apart, and parity runs always have rng_set. Contrast relic/astrolabe N1, which is a gap precisely because it has NO parity arm.
